newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 10.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 10.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money was traded at 10.0 percent on Thursday morning on sufficient liquidity.
Dealers said the market was well supplied following an early injection of 299 billion rupiah into the market.
One local bank dealer said longer-term rates were also trending down, with one-week and one-month money traded at 11.5 and 12.0 percent, respectively.
One-month money was last given at 12.5 percent.
He said operators appeared to be rather calm depsite the approaching month-end next week.

Dealers said they were not worried because there was nothing extraordinary scheduled for this month-end, compared with last week's new bank reserve requirement rate which had only a minor effect on the market.
The average overnight interbank rate on Wednesday was 11.48 percent, compared with 12.49 percent on Tuesday.
One treasurer said offshore interest in domestic bonds remained firm despite some nervousness in the foreign exchange market ahead of the start of the election campaign on Sunday.
"We see sustained interest. The only difference now is they are covering with swaps while they left it open in the past."
"I don't see any significant unloading," he added.
He expected the market to stabilise in the second week of election campaign.
The campaign for the May 29 parliamentary election will last from April 27 to May 23.
